text:
sara_sales: Quick heads-up — Acero (mid-market finance) wants a drop-in replacement for their current vendor but with stricter security, EU residency, and an easy 1:1 pricing mapping. Can we scope a short POC to validate parity and ops requirements?
ankit_se: Which endpoints are critical? chat completions, streaming, function-calls, or embeddings? Any nonstandard fields we should mirror?
mike_sre: Also: network/infra blockers up front — they require static egress IPs, mutual TLS, and an allowlist for a few CIDRs. Dedicated can handle static egress; hosted will need NAT partner.
nora_security: Please get their security questionnaire (SIG/SSQ). Also confirm BYOK/KMS needs: they mentioned HSM-backed keys and rotation audit logs — that's Private/Dedicated territory, not standard hosted.
kim_integration: From a behavior POV, we've seen parity gaps around tokenization, stop-sequence semantics, and function-call ordering. We can build a thin compatibility shim to canonicalize inputs and post-process outputs (strip vendor-specific metadata). Example shim ideas below.
ankit_se: On pricing: they bill per "message_unit" (combines prompt+response). They want a 1:1 billing mapping so their finance team doesn't refactor cost models. We'll need a sample traffic slice to compute token-to-message conversion and estimate monthly run rate.
sara_sales: I can request 48–72h sample logs and their current monthly spend. They also require SLA 99.95, 30-day retention policy, and EU-only data at rest.
mike_sre: 99.95 is possible with Reserved/Dedicated capacity + runbook and monthly commit. Hosted default SLA is 99.9. Note ops uplift and pricing delta for reserved capacity. Also need a runbook for failover to another region if EU region has issues.
nora_security: Flag: pen-test windows (they want a quarterly pentest window and embargoed disclosure rules). Also require contractual DPA + SOC2/ISO references — we have those but need to surface certs.
kim_integration: Shim sketch (python pseudo):
```
# compatibility shim example
resp = redwood_client.chat.create(prompt=prompt, max_tokens=600)
# remove vendor metadata and normalize choices
if 'meta' in resp: del resp['meta']
text = resp['choices'][0]['text'].rstrip('\n')
# rewrite function-call structure to match their schema
if 'function_call' in resp['choices'][0]:
    fc = resp['choices'][0]['function_call']
    fc['args'] = json.loads(fc.get('args', '{}'))
return { 'result': text, 'choice_index': 0 }
```
kim_integration: Also recommend normalizing stop sequences client-side and mapping streaming chunk events to their existing `on_delta` callbacks to preserve UX.
ankit_se: For parity testing we should build a small harness: replay ~500 representative prompts and compare top-k outputs and token counts. Kim: can you estimate how many prompts we need to show <5% behavioural delta?
kim_integration: I can run an initial 200-prompt smoke; for statistical confidence ~1000 is better. With that we can categorize deltas: tokenization, model response template, and semantic shifts. Postprocessing will handle a lot but some cases need model tuning or different model variant.
sara_sales: Next actions: (1) I will ask Acero for 72h sample logs + their SSQ by EOD tomorrow. (2) Schedule 30m tech call Wed 10am PT with @kim_integration and @nora_security. (3) Kim to prepare quick shim POC and initial 200-prompt test by Friday. (4) Mike to list egress options and rough cost uplift for reserved capacity.
mike_sre: I'll compile IPs, FQDNs, and reserved capacity pricing today.
nora_security: I'll draft the SSQ responses and outline gaps for BYOK/HSM and pen-test windows.
ankit_se: :thumbsup:
sara_sales: Thanks team — Acero is high priority but tight timeline. I'll update once I have logs.
devbot: POC repo created: git.redwood/pocts/acero-retrofit — bootstrap files + README.
